evaluation_heuristic: IMPLEMENTATION TASK. Implement the generic hierarchical evaluation runtime defined by runtime_spec. Treat runtime_spec as authoritative. Use config_skeleton and audit_js_skeleton as prescribed structural starting points: preserve the known algorithm and configurable surfaces, fill implementation mechanics, repair skeleton defects needed to satisfy the spec, and do not redesign the algorithm. Produce exactly two complete artifacts: ChatMachines/GeminiEvaluation/hierarchical-runtime/config.json and ChatMachines/GeminiEvaluation/hierarchical-runtime/audit.js. The runtime is generic; do not add GeminiSupervisor-audit-specific task semantics, requirement-evaluation semantics, or semantic context segmentation. Keep downstream task, criteria, response contracts, program return envelope, max_tokens value, and failed-b stopping threshold configurable where the supplied skeleton intentionally leaves them unset. B is controller state and its configured rule resolves every configurable iterator setting for that round. All evaluator calls occur after division and assignment to b. divider.max_tokens applies only to context assigned to a newly created b and is checked once at assignment; do not add request-size or retry context-size checks. Use tokens, never bytes/KB, for all sizing. All token counts must route through one runtime token-count function. Response size conditions are configured as divisors/ratios of max_tokens; intended initial hard threshold is max_tokens/2. Retries are finite ordered configured conditionals. Preserve the agreed defaults: system failure gets one fresh repeat of the original invocation, then failed b if the repeat fails; mechanically unacceptable response gets one fresh corrective invocation receiving assigned context + previous response + exact mechanical error + task + criteria + response contract, then retains the latest result/failure metadata if still unacceptable. Retries are sequential; the first successful attempt is retained and later attempts do not occur. A failed b stays visible in supervisory state but contributes no output to later context. The configured failed-b supervisory condition may stop the program after multiple failures. After each completed nonterminal round, aggregate only successful responses and sum their response token counts. The configured initial termination condition is aggregate_response_tokens <= divider.max_tokens. When it is satisfied, set terminal_round before advancing normally: increment B, resolve B config, divide, assign b, and evaluate normally. The resulting terminal round is expected to contain one b. After that terminal round completes, return immediately without another termination check, division, or evaluator call. There is no separate final evaluator branch. Preserve provenance through reductions. Configuration and evaluator outputs are declarative data interpreted only by predefined runtime operations. Use the supplied Gemini API interface/environment conventions appropriate to Node.js/GitHub Actions; do not embed secrets. Return complete, runnable, non-truncated file contents, not patches, pseudocode, Markdown fences, or ellipses. Account for every requirement ID from runtime_spec in implementation_mapping. Any requirement not fully implemented must also appear in requirements_not_implemented with an exact reason; silently omitted requirements are invalid. Before returning, verify that every spec requirement ID appears exactly once in implementation_mapping and that artifact contents are complete.
